title: Witness Points for Bernstein's Density Theorem

problemStatement.formal: For an infinite node sequence (x_k) in [-1,1], define the n-th Lebesgue function by \Lambda_n(x) = \sum_{k=1}^n |\ell_k^{(n)}(x)| for the Lagrange basis on x_1,...,x_n. Bernstein's density statement says the points with \Lambda_n(x)/\log n \to \infty are dense in [-1,1]. OQ-01 asks whether the Lean axioms bernstein_density_theorem or the weaker erdos_max_theorem, asserting a logarithmic lower bound for max_{[-1,1]} \Lambda_n, can be formalized from Mathlib rather than assumed.
problemStatement.plain: Investigate whether the approximation-theory axioms in Erdos1132Problem.lean can be reduced. The witness-point question is about points where the Lebesgue function for Lagrange interpolation grows as in Bernstein's dense-good-points theorem; the nearer target is a formal lower bound for the maximum Lebesgue function, possibly via Chebyshev tools or a concrete equidistant-node calculation.
